Singer Seth Anthony tells Danny Jones how eight years in prison created his music career in episode 30 of the KONCRETE podcast. Anthony's country-rap songs grew out of the writing and pain of his years inside. His story runs from bars to bars, cell bars to song bars.

Anthony describes finding his voice while locked up and the discipline prison forced on him. He explains how the songs he wrote inside became a living after release. Jones asks about the friends he lost and the ones still waiting. Inspired and musical listeners get a redemption tale with a soundtrack.
podcast-dannyjones-ao23Pmcx-K0:
Author James Rosone warns Danny Jones about China's new warships, AI weapons, and the road to a third world war. Rosone writes military thrillers grounded in heavy research on modern forces. His fiction doubles as a warning about where real rivalries may lead.

Rosone walks through China's naval build-up and what it means for the Pacific. He explains how AI-guided weapons could speed war beyond human control. Jones asks how a conflict might start and whether leaders see the risk clearly. Wary listeners get a novelist's informed nightmare, built from today's headlines and hardware.
podcast-joerogan-8S0cEV70NK0:
Michael Pollan's episode 1678 of the Joe Rogan Experience came years before psychedelics hit the mainstream news. Pollan, the food and nature writer, had just turned his reporting toward plant medicines. Rogan hosted him early in that run, and the talk has a fresh, curious tone.

Pollan lays out the careful, reported case for psychedelic therapy: what the trials showed, what the drugs do to a stuck mind, and where the risks sit. He speaks as a reporter, not a believer. Heard now, the episode marks the moment a fringe subject began its move into polite public debate.
podcast-joerogan-wo6K0Bav3K0:
Scholar Diana Pasulka joins Joe Rogan for episode 2533 of the Joe Rogan Experience. Pasulka is a professor of religious studies who writes on UFO belief as a form of faith. Her books draw on scientists who work in secret programs.

Pasulka and Rogan talk about how smart people in space work treat UFOs as a sacred topic. She shares tales from her field work with believers and with engineers. Rogan asks where faith ends and proof starts. Listeners get a scholar's calm take on the wildest topic on the show. The library keeps the episode as a record of her visit.
podcast-tuckercarlson-cWNd5CCejk0:
Paul Manafort, who first ran Donald Trump's campaign, joins Tucker Carlson to call the race. Asked who wins, he answers at once: Donald Trump. He sounds fully sure of the call.

Manafort breaks down the undecided voters who will decide the outcome. In southern battleground states, he says, they think the nation heads the wrong way. He draws on a career that began with the Ford campaign of 1976. The episode gives an old operative's clear-eyed map of a race, from voter mood to the states that matter most. Age has not dulled his eye for a race.
